ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Abu Simbel Temple is located 280 kilometers south of the Aswan Dam. It was built in 1257 BC by Ramesses II, a pharaoh of the 19th Dynasty of ancient Egypt, because of his worship of the sun god. The temple has a 61 m long tunnel, and a statue of the pharaoh stands at the end of the tunnel. Only on the early mornings of two specific days in a year can sunlight pass through the tunnel and shine on the statue of the pharaoh at the end. Read the figure and answer: <image1> If the two days when sunlight enters the end of the tunnel are regularly distributed in time within a year, and if Ramesses II's birthday is April 21, then which day is most likely the enthronement date he selected?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the temple tunnel is a fixed straight passage, and sunlight enters from the tunnel opening side along the tunnel axis, showing that only when the direction of the morning sunlight is consistent with the direction of the tunnel can sunlight pass through the tunnel and shine on the statue at the end. Then reason: The same fixed sunrise azimuth usually appears twice in a year before and after the summer solstice, and the two dates are approximately symmetrical about the summer solstice. It is known that one of the days is Ramesses II's birthday, April 21, and April 21 is before the summer solstice, about June 22. From April 21 to June 22 is about 62 days, so the other corresponding date should be about 62 days after the summer solstice. Counting about 62 days forward from June 22 gives August 23. Therefore the enthronement date he selected is most likely August 23.
